brief.headline: In Google's public GA4 sample, total revenue rose from 13150 to 26966 while sessions fell from 27707 to 27478, and the conversion spike must be verified before acting.
executive_summary: This brief uses Google's public obfuscated GA4 sample, not a real client.
Total revenue changed 105.1% and total transactions changed 58.1%, while total sessions changed -0.8%.
Total conversion rate changed from 0.82 to 1.36, but the payload flags conversion rate and revenue per session for tracking verification.
Referral campaign revenue was 16252 with a 175.6% change, while direct campaign revenue was 1033 with a -38.6% change.

what_changed.title: Total revenue and transactions rose
what_changed.detail: Revenue was 26966 versus 13150, a 105.1% change; transactions were 400 versus 253, a 58.1% change; sessions were 27478 versus 27707, a -0.8% change.

what_changed.title: Product view to add to cart weakened
what_changed.detail: Product view -> add to cart was 18.63 versus 22.45, a -17% change and -3.82 points; the payload lists it as the biggest leak.

what_changed.title: Direct traffic and revenue fell
what_changed.detail: Direct campaign users were 3596 versus 5040, a -28.7% change; direct campaign sessions were 3724 versus 5173, a -28% change; direct campaign revenue was 1033 with a -38.6% change.

what_changed.title: Referral campaign performance improved
what_changed.detail: Referral campaign revenue was 16252 with a 175.6% change; transactions were 246 with a 110.3% change; conversion rate was 3 with an 87.8% change.

likely_drivers: The revenue increase is likely consistent with stronger referral campaign performance, because referral campaign revenue was 16252 and changed 175.6%.
The revenue increase is likely consistent with a higher cart to checkout rate, which rose from 42.15 to 56.62, a 34.3% change.
The direct traffic decline is likely consistent with direct campaign sessions falling from 5173 to 3724, a -28% change.
risks: If the conversion rate and revenue per session spikes are tracking errors, the team may make decisions on inflated performance.
If product view -> add to cart remains the biggest leak, product interest may not become carts.
If direct traffic continues to fall, the sample may become more dependent on referral traffic.

actions.action: Verify GA4 purchase, revenue, and conversion tracking before using the conversion rate or revenue per session figures in planning.
actions.why: The payload marks these figures for tracking verification, so they are not a demand story until confirmed.
actions.evidence: revenue_per_session current 0.98 previous 0.47 change_pct 106.8 check_tracking true; conversion_rate current 1.36 previous 0.82 change_pct 66.6 check_tracking true

actions.action: Run one add-to-cart test on top product detail pages, starting with Google Cloud Unisex Zip Hoodie and Google Women's Striped L/S.
actions.why: The funnel shows the biggest leak at product view -> add to cart, and these items have high views and adds to cart.
actions.evidence: Product view -> add to cart current 18.63 previous 22.45 change_pct -17 change_points -3.82; Google Cloud Unisex Zip Hoodie views_cur 3186 adds_to_cart_cur 670; Google Women's Striped L/S views_cur 3267 adds_to_cart_cur 739

actions.action: Create a reactivation test for at-risk high value customers.
actions.why: The at-risk high value segment grew and has high historical spend, so a targeted CRM test can check whether it can be recovered.
actions.evidence: at_risk_high_value customers 470 previous 272 change 198; revenue_to_date 96564; avg_recency_days 62.6

data_caveats: Revenue per session and conversion rate have check_tracking true, so both figures must be verified before acting.
Source breakdowns should be treated with caution because 24.4% of sessions rows are unknown or obfuscated.
Calendar events are empty, so seasonality cannot be explained from the payload.
The data is Google's public obfuscated GA4 sample, not a real client.
